text:
maya: Heads-up — we're seeing unexpected p99 tail spikes on flashv3 after the kernel-tuner roll today. Started ~09:12UTC and affects some small-head models (head_dim around 20-24) with seqlen ~1k.
kevin: I noticed the alert. p50 unchanged, p95 up ~10ms, p99 up from ~120ms to ~430ms on some pods. KV-cache hit-rate seems fine.
anita: Repro'd locally with microbatch=1. Profiling indicates kernel picker oscillates between flashv3_causal and flashv2_noncausal across consecutive requests for the same workload. That causes full path switch and GPU synchronization spikes.
liu: Do you have the profiler logs?
manita: attaching pasted snippet from the trace (filtered):
```
[09:13:21.112] req=0x7f kernel_picker: selected flashv3_causal (headslice=22, seqlen=1024)
[09:13:21.189] runtime: launch flashv3 kernel (grid=..., sm=86)
[09:13:21.331] req=0x8 kernel_picker: selected flashv2_noncausal (headslice=24, seqlen=1024)
[09:13:21.409] runtime: fallback launch flashv2 kernel, sync
latency_ms: 72 -> 418 -> 76 -> 411 (pattern repeats)
```
kevin: That pattern smells like our chooser heuristics using head_dim % 8 alignment + a seqlen heuristic that flips when KV cache warmup changes observed sequence distribution. For head_dim=22 it sometimes rounds to 24 for flashv2 path.
manita: Exact repro command I used: 
```
./perf/run_local.sh --model=gpt-small --seq_len=1024 --batch_size=1 --head_dim=22 --profile=nvtx --repeat=200
```
bench-bot: perf-run 2460011222 completed: avg=85ms p95=140ms p99=410ms (env: sm86, cuda12)
ops-bot: deploy 2026-03-17T08:55:03Z: kernel-tuner v1.9 -> success on cluster A, rolled to 40% on cluster B
kevin: We pushed a subtle change to the tuner where we probe alternate kernels per-request when estimated throughput delta < 5%, to pick lower-memmoves for some seqlen windows. That probe looks too aggressive for small microbatch workloads.
liu: Could KV cache hit ratio hysteresis be used? If KV hit changes cause different memory traffic we should avoid probing mid-flight. Maybe require N consecutive requests with same pick before switching.
maya: Agree. Two mitigations: 1) quick rollback of the aggressive probe flag; 2) add hysteresis to kernel chooser (N=3 by default) + prefer stable pick when KV cache warmed. Which is faster?
anita: Rollback is fastest to mitigate. I can patch chooser to skip probes when microbatch==1 or head_dim % 8 != 0. That's a quick guard.
kevin: Also let's add a telemetry tag on kernel switches so we can chart switch rate per pod. If we see >1 switch/sec that's bad.
liu: For longer-term, we should tune the cost model to include a KV-cache locality term and a sticky penalty for switching that decays over 5s.
maya: Action items: anita -> revert probe flag + patch guard (hotfix) (ETA 30m). kevin -> add metric for kernel_switch_rate and a dashboard tile (ETA 2h). liu -> design sticky penalty param and add to tracker (ETA end of week). I'll open a short postmortem draft after we stabilize.
kevin: One gotcha: rollback will remove some wins for aligned heads on batch>4. We'll gate rollback to microbatch and head_dim range to avoid losing those wins.
anita: Patch ready, testing on canary. Quick test shows p99 back to ~130ms for the repro case.
maya: Thanks — keep updating thread. We'll schedule a 9:45UTC quick sync if the canary is green. :thumbsup:
